checks.name: Authoritative On-Chain Vote Count vs. Off-Chain Displayed Tally
checks.expected: All displayed candidate vote counts match smart contract storage exactly
checks.explanation: Smart contract storage is the sole cryptographic source of truth. Any deviation indicates database desynchronization, unconfirmed local edits, or off-chain data tampering.

checks.name: Event Log Tally Reconstruction vs. Contract Storage
checks.expected: Sum of VoteCasted events matches candidate stored voteCount
checks.actual: 1 vote events successfully reconciled with contract storage.
checks.explanation: Every valid vote transaction emits an indexed VoteCasted event on the Ethereum ledger. Reconstructing the ledger independent of state variables verifies internal contract consistency.

checks.name: Aggregate Vote Count Mathematical Sanity
checks.expected: Total votes equals sum of candidate votes (1)
checks.actual: Contract aggregate total: 1, Sum of candidates: 1
checks.explanation: Validates that the smart contract internal tally accumulator matches the sum of individual candidate buckets.

checks.name: Cryptographic Transaction Receipts & Block Inclusion
checks.expected: All recorded vote transactions exist on Ethereum with status=1 (Mined & Successful)
checks.explanation: Having a transaction hash does not guarantee the ballot was counted; the Ethereum EVM receipt status must be strictly 1 (Success).

checks.name: One-Person-One-Vote Cryptographic Constraint
checks.expected: Each registered voter address appears at most once in verified vote events
checks.actual: 1 unique voting accounts across 1 vote events (0 duplicates).
checks.explanation: Guarantees that no address was able to submit more than one ballot on the blockchain ledger.

checks.name: Election Lifecycle State Synchronization
checks.expected: Smart contract status (1) matches persistent database status
checks.explanation: Verifies that administrative open/close transitions are uniformly recognized by both the blockchain state and the backend coordinator.

limitations: Local Hardhat development network timestamps advance with transactions, not real-world seconds.
Audit validates cryptographic state against current block height; historical events require archive node availability.
Hardware sensor physical impedance attacks cannot be detected via blockchain state inspection alone.
